Subject: Break-glass: Stabilize Close Trajectory — CloudHealth MAP & risk heatmap

Team —

Quick summary up front: CloudHealth is signalling a one-week push to their acceptance window due to an internal procurement review and an SSO configuration gating item. This is a critical-account ask: slipping the go-live by a week materially increases churn risk on the current pilot and pushes their renewal cadence into a tighter fiscal window.

I need a tight, executable mitigation plan by EOD today that does three things:
- Document the delta in the MAP (what slips, who owns the impacted milestones).
- Put a short-term SLA/credit option on the table for procurement to keep momentum.
- Escalate to Sales leadership if we cannot hold a target go-live within seven calendar days.

Attached: brief heatmap + current MAP (MAP_CloudHealth_v4.pdf, close_risk_heatmap_Q2.xlsx).

Ask: Grace, can you produce a 48-hour re-baselined MAP with owner reassignments and a clear gating checklist? Priyom, can you confirm DocuSign/PO status and whether procurement will accept a staged signature (agreement now, final SOW after cutover)? Laura, please prepare an up-level note for Sales Ops to flag this as a potential executive escalation if EOD remediation items aren't met. Jonas — keep watch on infra capacity in case we need a burst window during cutover.

I'll consolidate and escalate if answers don't converge.

— Markus

Markus —

Thanks for the heads up. I ran a quick re-baseline and attached a cleaned MAP with explicit owners and three contingency lanes: 
1) Keep planned cutover date, offer limited rollback window + engineering on-call for 48 hours (owner: Jonas)
2) Move cutover +7 days with fixed acceptance window and fixed onboarding resources (owner: Grace)
3) Phased go-live: subset of services day 0, remainder day 7 (owner: Priyom)

Key gating checklist (short):
- SSO cert exchange validated (CloudHealth action item)
- Provisioning role matrix finalized (internal)
- DocuSign signature in principal (procurement)
- Final data retention & audit clause accepted (legal)

I'm attaching: MAP_CloudHealth_v4.pdf (updated with owners) and close_risk_heatmap_Q2.xlsx (heatmap with impact bands). I recommend we propose the phased go-live to procurement as the least-risk option.

If procurement is inflexible on dates we should surface the SLA/credit option as a commercial concession to keep the trial momentum.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
